scenes.title: The explanation fits too well
scenes.viewerPurpose: Coherence Pressure proposes a name for the pull to connect things before the evidence is there.
scenes.composition: Two observations sit apart on a source record while a proposed connection hovers between them.
addOrChange: Keep the bridge visibly proposed; no proof tick or diagnosis label; shorten the opening record text.

cues.visualAction: Show the two observations first, then the attractive proposed connection marked as a question.
Reveal the concrete app-removal and video-watching observations beside the child’s tablet.

scenes.title: Two ordinary observations
scenes.viewerPurpose: A model finds a way to connect the two through attention and choice.
scenes.composition: A child uses a tablet while a separate note offers one possible explanation.
addOrChange: Remove repetitive feed swaps and extra parent gestures; avoid making this a claim about the child’s psychology.

cues.visualAction: Let the explanation join the two observations on paper, without changing the child’s actions.
Pause over the question beside that joining strip; leave the link uncertain.

scenes.title: A connection still to prove
scenes.viewerPurpose: The book examines how convincing connections can appear before anyone has tested them.
scenes.composition: The explanatory connection becomes an object the reader can inspect.
addOrChange: Remove the settled avoidance/exploration labels, which give away analysis before the viewer reads it.

cues.visualAction: Lift the connection slightly away from the observations so it can be questioned separately.
Place the proposed term on the same page under an unanswered check, treating the book’s own idea equally.

scenes.title: Before the story closes
scenes.viewerPurpose: For people who think and write with AI, the original conversation makes the problem easy to recognize.
scenes.composition: The original conversation stays beside the polished explanation.
addOrChange: Remove benchmark diagrams and multiple case outcomes; keep one comparison and a reading cue.

cues.visualAction: Bring the original conversation and its later explanation together for comparison.
Hold the reader’s finger between them while the book remains open to the source case.

checks: Do not generate voice until all122 script and visual plans pass review.
Use only source-grounded diagrams and neutral illustrative examples; preserve uncertainty and proposal labels.
Measure audio and keep the complete film at or below120 seconds without accelerating narration.
Inspect Color, Light and Dark at desktop and phone sizes; verify captions, labels and cue timing.
Listening review and visual QA are separate from having a compiled film.
